text: I understand you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; to determine the cause of these concerning systemic and localizing symptoms, where exactly is your abdominal pain located and how would you describe its severity?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the location of your abdominal pain will help distinguish between potential causes like lymphoma versus other malignancies. Has your abdominal pain radiated anywhere else, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite besides the weight loss?

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT confirms massive involvement of cervical, axillary, and mediastinal lymph nodes, which is highly suggestive of a systemic lymphoma or metastatic carcinoma. To differentiate between lymphoma subtypes and rule out other causes, do you have a known history of HIV, or do you recall any recent infections? REQUEST TEST: HIV Antigen/Antibody, T-Cell Subset Analysis, and Flow Cytometry on lymph node biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The flow cytometry results showing CD20 positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index confirm a B-cell lineage malignancy, which fits the clinical picture of systemic "B symptoms" and massive lymphadenopathy seen on CT.
